events.title: Anointed at the Gihon Spring
events.subtitle: A son who rode down on David's mule
story: David was old. Even piled with blankets he could not keep warm, and Abishag the Shunammite cared for him at his side. Meanwhile Prince Adonijah, born after Absalom, put himself forward, saying, “I will be king.” Adonijah got himself chariots and horsemen and fifty men to run ahead of him, and Joab and the priest Abiathar followed him. A feast was held beside the spring of En-rogel, but Nathan, Benaiah and Solomon were not invited.

The prophet Nathan went to Solomon's mother Bathsheba and said, “Adonijah has become king, and our lord David doesn't know it.” Bathsheba went into the king's room, bowed down and said, “Did you not swear that my son Solomon would succeed you?” Nathan came in too and told him the same thing. The old king spoke: “As surely as the Lord lives, who has rescued me from every trouble, today I will do just as I swore.”

Mounted on David's mule, Solomon went down to the Gihon Spring. The priest Zadok took the horn of oil from the tabernacle and poured it on Solomon's head. The trumpet sounded and the people shouted, “Long live King Solomon!” The sound of the pipes and the shouting was enough to split the ground, and Adonijah's guests scattered in fear. David bowed in worship on his bed and said, “Praise the Lord, the God of Israel, who has given someone to sit on my throne today and let my own eyes see it.”

words.text: As surely as the Lord lives, who has rescued me from every trouble: today I will do exactly what I swore to you, that your son Solomon would be king after me.
Praise the Lord, the God of Israel. Today he has given someone to sit on my throne, and has let my own eyes see it.
May my lord King David live forever!
Amen. As the Lord has been with my lord the king, so may he be with Solomon, and make his throne even greater than the throne of King David.

events.note: The Gihon Spring is Jerusalem's main spring, rising on the slope of the Kidron Valley east of the City of David. En-rogel, where Adonijah held his feast, lay a little to the south, close enough that the shouting at Gihon could be heard there.
events.reflect: Of the promises I have long put off, which one should I keep today?

quiz.q: What did Solomon ride when he went down to the Gihon Spring to be anointed?
quiz.explain: David ordered that Solomon be set on his own mule, taken down to Gihon and anointed there (1 Kgs 1:33, 38).

events.title: Preparing for the Temple
events.subtitle: Gathering for a house he would never build
story: Pointing to the threshing floor of Araunah, David said, “Here is where the house of the Lord God will stand.” From that day David gathered stonecutters to dress the stone and piled up iron and more bronze than could be weighed. The people of Sidon and Tyre brought cedar beyond counting. David said, “My son Solomon is young and inexperienced. The house of the Lord must be renowned throughout the world, so I will make preparations for it now.”

David called Solomon and said, “My son, I wanted to build a house for the name of the Lord. But the Lord said to me, You have shed much blood and fought great wars, so you will not build my house. A son will be born to you who will be a man of peace; he will build it.” Later, before all the leaders of Israel, David handed Solomon the plans for the temple that the Lord had made clear to him, and said, “Be strong and courageous, and do the work.”

From his own treasure David gave three thousand talents of gold from Ophir and seven thousand talents of silver. The leaders gave willingly too, and the people rejoiced at what had been given wholeheartedly. Before the whole assembly David praised the Lord: “Who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to give like this? Everything comes from you, and we have given you only what came from your hand. Our days on earth are like a shadow.”

words.text: A son will be born to you who will be a man of peace. He will build a house for my name. He will be my son, and I will be his father.
My son Solomon, know the God of your father, and serve him with your whole heart and a willing mind. If you seek him, he will let himself be found by you.
Who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to give like this? Everything comes from you, and we have given you only what we received from your hand.
Be strong and courageous, and do the work. Don't be afraid. The Lord my God is with you, and he will not leave you until all the work is finished.

events.note: Chronicles records that David provided a hundred thousand talents of gold and a million talents of silver for the temple. A talent is estimated at about thirty kilograms. Psalm 30 carries the heading “A song at the dedication of the house.”
events.reflect: Even if I won't see the fruit, can I gladly prepare the way for those who come after me?

quiz.q: Why did God not let David build the temple?
options: He was a man of war who had shed much blood
quiz.explain: Because David had shed much blood and fought great wars, God did not let him build the temple, but had his son Solomon, a man of peace, build it (1 Chr 22:8–9; 28:3).

events.title: David's Last Words
events.subtitle: A last breath that sang of a cloudless morning
story: The boy who had tended sheep was now an old king with white hair. David son of Jesse, the singer of Israel, sang his last song: “The Spirit of the Lord speaks through me; his word is on my tongue. The Rock of Israel said to me: One who rules people justly, ruling in the fear of God, is like the light of sunrise on a cloudless morning, like new grass springing from the earth after rain.”

David went on singing: “Is not my house like this before God? He has made an everlasting covenant with me, ordered in every part and kept secure.” As the day of his death drew near, David called Solomon and charged him: “I am going the way of all the earth. Be strong, and show yourself a man. Walk in the Lord's ways, as it is written in the law of Moses. Then the Lord will keep his promise that you will never lack a descendant to sit on the throne.”

After giving his instructions one by one, about Joab and Shimei and about the kindness to be shown to the sons of Barzillai, David rested with his ancestors and was buried in the City of David. He was a king who reigned forty years in all: seven years in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem. Psalm 72 closes with a single line: the prayers of David son of Jesse are ended. For a long time Israel waited for the king from his line who would rise like a cloudless morning.

words.text: One who rules people justly, who rules in the fear of God, is like the light of sunrise on a cloudless morning, like new grass springing from the earth after rain.
The Spirit of the Lord speaks through me; his word is on my tongue.
He has made an everlasting covenant with me, a covenant ordered in every part and kept secure.
I am going the way of all the earth. Be strong, and show yourself a man. Keep what the Lord your God has entrusted to you, and walk in his ways.

events.note: The seven years in Hebron were when he was king over the tribe of Judah alone. For a long time afterward the prophets awaited a righteous branch to spring from the house of David, and the New Testament calls Jesus “the son of David.”

quiz.explain: David reigned over Israel forty years in all: seven years in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem (1 Kgs 2:11).

ui.gospel:
God loved the world so much that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him will not perish but have eternal life. (John 3:16)
We had turned from God to go our own way and were lost in sin, but Jesus carried that sin for us, died on the cross, and rose again on the third day. (1 Cor 15:3–4)
To all who believe in him and receive him, he gives the right to become children of God. (John 1:12)

ui.blessing:
The Lord is my shepherd; I have all that I need.
He lets me lie down in green pastures and leads me beside quiet waters. (Ps 23:1–2)
May the one who called the boy in the fields call your name too, and may the one who was with him through the nights of flight guard your way.

ui.invite:
If the Jesus you met on this way has stayed with you, visit a church near you. We hope you will meet God in worship and in his word, and know the blessing of being adopted as his child — calling God "Father". (Rom 8:15)
He is still standing at the door, waiting for you. (Rev 3:20)
ui.prayer: Jesus, I believe that you came to this earth because you love me, and that you carried the cross for me. Please be the Lord of my life, and receive me as a child of God. Amen.
